cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: The woman was among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before returning to Australia in recent months.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining the Islamic State following her return from Syria, where she had been detained in a camp for years.

The woman is among several groups of women and children who have recently returned to Australia after extended stays in Syrian detention facilities. These camps housed family members of suspected Islamic State fighters.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The government is allowing people to connect with the world again, though access remains limited and uncertain.
cards.body:
Iran's government has begun restoring internet access after imposing a near-total shutdown that lasted 88 days. The blackout had cut off most Iranians from global online communication and news.

Access remains partial, with not everyone able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the government will allow it to continue, creating an atmosphere of temporary and conditional connectivity.

cards.headline: California poll shows Becerra opening lead in governor's race
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra has pulled ahead in polling as the California gubernatorial election approaches.
cards.body:
A new poll indicates Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in California's gubernatorial race. The candidates have been making campaign stops across the state, including recent appearances in the Bay Area.

The race has shifted rapidly in recent weeks, according to political observers. Democratic Party officials say they are not concerned about the outcome of the gubernatorial contest. Voter guides are being published to help undecided Californians understand the race as the election nears.

cards.headline: Chinese factories expand overseas operations globally
cards.teaser: China is establishing manufacturing facilities in other countries as its trade surplus triggers international concern.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are building factories across the world as the country's massive trade surplus creates tension with trading partners. China's trade surplus reached $1.2 trillion, prompting questions about how Beijing manages its international economic relationships.

The expansion of Chinese manufacturing abroad has raised concerns among competitors in various countries. India may benefit from the shift in global manufacturing patterns. A former Chongqing mayor called for action as China appears poised for a record trade surplus this year.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker will begin customer deliveries of its new SUV model next month.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. The company has finally announced a firm date for these initial deliveries.

CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as potentially the most important product Rivian has launched to date, underscoring the vehicle's significance to the company's future lineup.

cards.headline: SEC commissioner defends conference superiority despite Big Ten's recent dominance
cards.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said his conference still stands alone as the best in college football, even as the Big Ten has won the past three national championships and holds a 4-0 record against the SEC in College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Sankey made the remarks during college football's spring meetings, a gathering that has been dominated by discussions of conference expansion and playoff structure. His comments come at a time when the Big Ten has demonstrated clear superiority in head-to-head competition.

The SEC has long positioned itself as the premier conference in college football, but recent results have challenged that narrative. The Big Ten's three consecutive national titles represent a significant shift in the sport's power dynamics.

Sankey's insistence that the SEC remains the top conference by far appears to dismiss the on-field evidence from recent seasons. The head-to-head playoff record and championship outcomes provide measurable data points that contradict his assessment.

The spring meetings have brought conference realignment and competitive balance to the forefront of college football governance. As conferences continue to expand and reshape the sport's landscape, the competitive rivalry between the SEC and Big Ten has intensified.

Sankey's defense of SEC supremacy reflects the high stakes involved in maintaining the conference's brand and recruiting advantages. Conference reputation directly impacts television revenue, recruiting, and playoff selection.

The broader context includes ongoing negotiations over playoff expansion and format. How conferences position themselves in these discussions could determine the future structure of college football's postseason.

While Sankey maintains the SEC's dominance, the Big Ten's recent success in championship games and playoff matchups suggests the balance of power in college football may be shifting. The coming seasons will determine whether the Big Ten's run continues or if the SEC can reclaim its position atop the sport.

cards.headline: Phillies pitcher breaks franchise scoreless innings record set in 1911
cards.teaser: Cristopher Sanchez extended his scoreless streak to 44 innings, surpassing Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander's Phillies record.
cards.body:
Cristopher Sánchez set a new Phillies franchise record on Wednesday by extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, a record that had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's accomplishment breaks a benchmark that endured for over a century, solidifying his place in franchise history alongside one of baseball's greatest pitchers.

cards.headline: Spielberg opposes AI in creative filmmaking decisions
cards.body:
Director Steven Spielberg expressed opposition to using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson. Spielberg said he does not want AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood.

The director distinguished between AI applications he supports and those he opposes. He said he believes AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues.

Spielberg stated his objection to AI involvement in creative decisions. He said he does not support AI being used as the final word on anything creative in filmmaking. The director drew a clear boundary on where AI should not be applied in the entertainment industry.

The podcast appearance marks the latest instance of a major Hollywood figure weighing in on AI use in entertainment production. Spielberg has directed numerous films over several decades and remains an influential voice in the industry.

The director's comments come as the entertainment industry continues to debate the appropriate role of artificial intelligence in content creation. Production companies and studios have been exploring various AI applications, while creators and unions have raised concerns about the technology's impact on creative work.

Spielberg did not elaborate on specific AI tools or applications beyond his general opposition to the technology making creative decisions. He focused his objection on AI serving as a decision-making authority in creative matters rather than as a tool supporting human creators.

cards.headline: Senate Republican leaders endorse Ken Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders moved to unite behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Sen. John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone before publicly endorsing him on a radio show, signaling party unity after a divisive primary fight between Paxton and Sen. John Cornyn.

Republican leaders are emphasizing to major donors that winning Texas is critical to maintaining Senate control in the upcoming November elections. The effort represents an attempt to move past the bitter primary campaign and present a unified front heading into the general election.

cards.headline: Sen. Andy Kim responds to Homeland Security secretary over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Sen. Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized the senator for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin said Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim said the incident was never about him personally. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement and conditions at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by the president's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump, telling CBS News she thought he might have suffered a stroke.

"I was frightened, because I had never, ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Jill Biden said in comments set to air on Sunday. She described being alarmed by his faltering performance during the televised encounter.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
FIFA is facing an investigation by the attorneys general of New York and New Jersey over its 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe examines allegations that fans were misled about ticket purchases and seat locations.

The investigation centers on whether FIFA violated consumer protection standards in how it marketed and sold tickets for World Cup matches. The inquiry was launched following reports from fans who received different seats than expected or encountered unclear pricing structures.

cards.headline: Space stocks rally as SpaceX IPO approaches
cards.teaser: Companies like Rocket Lab and AST saw sharp gains ahead of SpaceX's planned public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX is moving forward with plans for a major stock market debut valued at $1.75 trillion, which could make Elon Musk a trillionaire. The anticipated IPO has generated increased interest across the space sector, with related stocks experiencing gains.

The race toward SpaceX's public offering comes as competition intensifies in the tech industry, particularly around AI development. Investors are closely monitoring the IPO's progress and SpaceX's investor pitch, which includes ambitious plans like Mars colonization.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe photographed Mars, including views of the south pole, while traveling toward an asteroid destination.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby en route to its primary destination, a distant asteroid. The mission took advantage of the planet encounter to capture high-resolution images offering unique views of the red planet.

The images include detailed photographs of Mars' south pole. NASA described the views as spectacular, with the spacecraft gathering data while traveling along its trajectory toward the asteroid target.

cards.headline: Google AI tools struggle with basic spelling tasks
cards.teaser: The company's artificial intelligence systems are having difficulty spelling words including the company's own name.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence features are experiencing significant spelling problems, unable to correctly spell basic words including "Google" itself, "disregard," "stop," and "ignore." The issues have become increasingly visible to users of the company's AI-powered search tools, with the AI Overview feature appearing to perform noticeably worse in recent times.

The spelling difficulties have attracted widespread online attention and represent an embarrassing setback for the tech giant's AI capabilities, raising questions about the reliability of these tools for everyday tasks.

cards.headline: Oklahoma athletic director sees playoff expansion as path to revive Bedlam rivalry
cards.teaser: Roger Denny said College Football Playoff expansion could enable tougher nonconference scheduling and potentially restore the Oklahoma-Oklahoma State series.
cards.body:
Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny said playoff expansion could create opportunities for scheduling stronger nonconference games and potentially reviving the Bedlam rivalry against Oklahoma State. The annual series between the in-state rivals has been discontinued.

Denny suggested that an expanded playoff format might reduce the risks associated with scheduling difficult nonconference opponents. This could make it feasible to restore traditional rivalry games that were dropped due to conference realignment and scheduling constraints.

cards.headline: Von Miller lobbies Broncos for return to Denver
cards.teaser: The former Super Bowl MVP said he will play in 2026 and has already contacted Sean Payton about rejoining his former team.
cards.body:
Von Miller said Wednesday he is "for sure" playing football in the 2026 season and has already reached out to Denver coach Sean Payton about returning to the Broncos. Miller spent much of his career with Denver before playing for other teams.

The Super Bowl MVP winner remains one of the franchise's most accomplished players. His outreach to Payton signals his interest in potentially reuniting with his former team.

cards.headline: Arizona forward Koa Peat stays in NBA draft
cards.teaser: The projected first-round pick will not return to college basketball, sources told ESPN.
cards.body:
Arizona forward Koa Peat is staying in the NBA draft rather than returning to college basketball. The projected first-round pick made his decision official on Wednesday, according to ESPN sources.

By keeping his name in the draft, Peat is forgoing the opportunity to maintain his college eligibility and pursue a professional career instead.

cards.headline: Film Obsession posts rare second-weekend box office increase
cards.teaser: The horror film achieved a second-weekend box office spike, a performance not seen since Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
The film Obsession posted a box office increase in its second weekend of release, becoming a breakout hit. The performance marked a rare achievement for theatrical releases.

The second-weekend spike represented a pattern not seen at the box office since Sound of Freedom. Multiple entertainment outlets described the film's performance as making history and becoming a record-breaking horror release.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight wins fourth consecutive News Emmy
cards.teaser: ABC World News Tonight With David Muir took the outstanding live news program prize for the fourth year in a row.
cards.body:
ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmy ceremony, the most of any outlet. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir received the outstanding live news program award, marking its fourth consecutive win in the category.

National Geographic won seven News Emmys, the second-highest total. The Nat Geo program Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller accounted for the bulk of those wins. Both ABC News and National Geographic are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Morris Day denies participation in National Mall Freedom 250 concert
cards.teaser: The musician said he and the Time will not perform at the June event despite being listed in the official lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied that he and the Time will perform at a Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall, calling reports of his participation rumors. Organizers had announced him as a headliner for a June 27 show as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

The event has generated debate among fans and performers. Other acts advertised for the celebration include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, C+C Music Factory, and Milli Vanilli. The concert is part of a celebration marking America's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Student journalist criticizes CBS News in scholarship acceptance speech
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos used his Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship acceptance to address CBS News editorial direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School, addressed CBS News during his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy ceremony. Campos said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

The Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship is named after the longtime CBS journalist. Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award to Campos at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Tipping expectations increase in US and abroad
cards.teaser: Service workers in the US now expect 20 percent tips as the practice spreads to other countries.
cards.body:
Tipping culture in the United States has intensified, with service workers expressing dissatisfaction when gratuities fall below 20 percent. The trend is also expanding to other countries where tipping was previously less common or expected at lower rates.

The shift reflects changing norms around compensation for service industry employees. Workers in restaurants and other service positions increasingly rely on tips as a significant portion of their income, leading to higher baseline expectations for what customers should pay beyond the listed price.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The Nintendo 64 game will join the subscription service's library on June 3.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will be added to Nintendo Switch Online next week. The game will become available to subscribers on June 3.

The addition expands the Nintendo 64 library available through the Switch Online service's Expansion Pack tier. Donkey Kong 64 originally released in the 1990s and is being added to the growing collection of classic N64 titles available to subscribers.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism of recent clothing choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed backlash over outfits that internet commenters said infantilized and sexualized her.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo commented on public reaction to her recent clothing selections. Internet commenters had accused her outfits of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer.

Rodrigo said people should not be responsible for others sexualizing them. The singer addressed the debate over her fashion choices directly in response to the online criticism.

cards.headline: Leonora Carrington psychiatric confinement painting to be exhibited publicly
cards.teaser: A work by the artist created during psychiatric confinement will be shown for the first time.
cards.body:
A painting by artist Leonora Carrington created during a period of psychiatric confinement will go on public display. The work has not been exhibited before.

Carrington was a surrealist artist and writer. The exhibition marks the first time this particular work from her confinement period will be shown to the public.

cards.headline: The Beaches song surges 888 percent after appearing in Off Campus
cards.teaser: The band's 2023 track Edge of the Earth went viral again following its use in a scene from the show.
cards.body:
Canadian band The Beaches saw their 2023 song Edge of the Earth experience an 888 percent increase in streaming. The spike followed the song's inclusion in a scene from the show Off Campus.

The track was featured in a scene involving characters Hannah and Garrett. This marks another viral moment for the band, which has previously gained attention through online platforms.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI platform
cards.teaser: The oncology-focused artificial intelligence company secured Series B funding led by Battery Ventures.
cards.body:
Triomics has secured $22 million in Series B funding to advance its artificial intelligence platform designed for oncology applications. Battery Ventures led the investment round.

The company is developing AI technology tailored specifically for cancer centers, with the new capital supporting continued development and deployment of its oncology-focused tools.

cards.headline: Top transfer portal player withdraws from NBA draft
cards.teaser: Milan Momcilovic, formerly of Iowa State, will return to college basketball instead of pursuing a professional career.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, the top-ranked player available in the transfer portal, has withdrawn from the NBA draft and will return to college basketball for the upcoming season. The former Iowa State forward made the decision through his agents, according to ESPN.

Momcilovic's choice to remain in college rather than pursue the professional ranks marks a significant development in the current transfer portal cycle, as he was the most coveted uncommitted player available to programs nationwide.

cards.headline: Music executive Larry Jackson sues to identify website operator
cards.teaser: The executive says an anonymous figure is running defamatory websites targeting him.
cards.body: Larry Jackson, a music executive associated with Kanye West's label, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person. Jackson

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to supply Patriot interceptors
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and Congress to provide Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. Zelensky said Ukraine has achieved significant success in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The request comes

hero.headline: US strikes Iran for second time this week despite ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States conducted new strikes on military targets in southern Iran on Wednesday, marking the second attack in three days while a ceasefire between the two countries remains officially in place. Both nations are simultaneously engaged in peace negotiations aimed at ending the three-month conflict.

A US official confirmed the strikes targeted attack drones and a drone ground control station, describing the military action as a self-defense measure. The attacks occurred near the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway critical to global energy supplies that handles roughly one-fifth of the world's oil transport.

Oil prices rose immediately following news of the strikes. The Trump administration has denied reaching any agreement with Iran regarding passage through the strategic waterway.

The fresh military action threatens the fragile ceasefire that both countries have maintained during diplomatic talks. The strikes represent a pattern of continued US military operations that risk undermining peace efforts, even as negotiators from both sides work toward a comprehensive agreement.

The military site targeted in the strikes underscores their strategic importance. The narrow Strait of Hormuz serves as a chokepoint for global energy supplies, making the region's security a matter of international concern beyond US-Iran relations alone.

Iran had imposed a near-total internet shutdown lasting 88 days during the conflict. The government recently began allowing citizens to reconnect with the outside world, though access remains limited and uncertain. Many Iranians remain unsure how long the restored connectivity will persist.

The pattern of military strikes followed by continued diplomatic negotiations illustrates the unstable nature of the current ceasefire. While military commanders conduct operations they view as necessary for national security, diplomatic teams continue working toward a permanent resolution.

Neither the US government nor Iran has publicly stated how the latest strikes will affect ongoing peace talks. The renewed military action raises significant questions about whether the ceasefire can remain stable long enough for negotiators to reach an agreement that would end the war.

The strikes come after a three-month period of conflict between the two countries. Previous US military operations occurred just days earlier, making Wednesday's attack the latest in a series of operations that complicate diplomatic efforts. Both governments have characterized the ceasefire as fragile, acknowledging the difficulty of maintaining peace while military operations continue.

The timing and location of these strikes demonstrate how security concerns continue to drive military decisions even as political leaders pursue negotiations. The international community, particularly nations dependent on Middle Eastern oil supplies, watches closely as the situation develops.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations across southern Lebanon as fighting intensifies
cards.teaser: The Israeli military declared areas south of the Zahrani River to be combat zones and warned of fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
The Israeli military has ordered residents to evacuate large areas of southern Lebanon south of the Zahrani River, designating these regions as active combat zones. The evacuation directive comes as the military threatens fresh strikes against Hezbollah targets in the area.

The escalating orders and military threats represent a significant intensification of hostilities between Israel and the Lebanese militant group, even as diplomatic efforts continue to address the broader regional conflict.

cards.headline: Australia files $2 billion lawsuit against 3M over contaminated defense sites
cards.teaser: The government is suing the US manufacturer over chemicals in firefighting foam that contaminated military installations.
cards.body:
The Australian government has launched its largest legal claim ever, seeking more than A$2 billion in damages from multinational manufacturer 3M. The lawsuit addresses contamination at defense bases caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) used in firefighting foam.

Known as "forever chemicals," PFAS persist indefinitely in the environment and the human body. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the legal action against 3M over the chemical contamination at Australian military installations.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting months after war declaration
cards.teaser: Neither side appears ready to back down despite mediation efforts by China.
cards.body:
Pakistan declared "open war" on Afghanistan months ago, and neither side has shown signs of backing down. The conflict remains active with no immediate resolution in sight.

China has attempted to mediate between the two countries but has not succeeded in brokering peace. The dispute reflects long-standing tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan that have proven resistant to diplomatic intervention.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: The woman was among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before returning to Australia in recent months.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining the Islamic State following her return from Syria, where she had been detained in a camp for years.

The woman is among several groups of women and children who have recently returned to Australia after extended stays in Syrian detention facilities. These camps housed family members of suspected Islamic State fighters.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading using internal data
cards.teaser: The longtime worker allegedly made $1.2 million on bets using information from inside the company.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with fraud for allegedly using confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and reportedly made $1.2 million in profits.

Prosecutors allege that Spagnuolo knew the outcomes of these bets before the public because he had access to Google's confidential data about search trends. The case underscores how employees with access to proprietary information face serious legal consequences when exploiting that advantage for personal financial gain.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The government is allowing people to connect with the world again, though access remains limited and uncertain.
cards.body:
Iran's government has begun restoring internet access after imposing a near-total shutdown that lasted 88 days. The blackout had cut off most Iranians from global online communication and news.

Access remains partial, with not everyone able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the government will allow it to continue, creating an atmosphere of temporary and conditional connectivity.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by the president's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump, telling CBS News she thought he might have suffered a stroke.

"I was frightened, because I had never, ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Jill Biden said in comments set to air on Sunday. She described being alarmed by his faltering performance during the televised encounter.

hero.headline: U.S. strikes Iran for second time in three days amid fragile ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States carried out a second round of military strikes against Iranian targets, hitting a drone launch site near the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes occurred during ongoing negotiations between the two countries aimed at ending a three-month war.

An official confirmed the U.S. military action targeted Iranian military positions. President Trump denied reports of any agreement with Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining what officials described as maximum demands on Iran during the diplomatic talks.

The strikes come as a ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran remains in place, though officials characterize it as fragile. Oil prices rose following news of the latest military action, reflecting market concerns about potential disruption to shipping lanes in the strategically important strait.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical passage for global oil shipments. Military activity in the region has heightened concerns about energy supplies and broader regional stability.

Negotiations to resolve the conflict continue despite the military strikes. Officials have not provided details about the substance of the talks or what specific demands the U.S. has presented to Iran.

The first U.S. strikes occurred three days before the latest action. The timing of the second strike, during active negotiations, signals the complexity of the diplomatic and military situation between the two countries.

The three-month war has drawn international attention to the Persian Gulf region. The combination of ongoing talks and continued military strikes reflects the uncertain path toward a potential resolution of the conflict.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA officer with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Prosecutors say a former CIA official stole 300 gold bars from the agency.
cards.body:
Federal authorities arrested David Rush, a former CIA officer, after discovering approximately $40 million worth of gold bars at his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole 300 gold bars from the agency.

The FBI executed the arrest following an investigation into the missing gold. According to charging documents, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. Sources familiar with the case confirmed the substantial quantity of gold recovered from his residence.

cards.headline: Paper mill disaster in Longview may be deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington history
cards.teaser: Two people are confirmed dead and nine remain missing after a chemical vat implosion at a Longview facility.
cards.body:
A chemical tank ruptured at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview on Tuesday morning, killing two workers and leaving nine others missing and presumed dead. One person died after being hospitalized following the disaster.

Washington's governor called it a potential deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. The incident involved white liquor, a caustic chemical used in paper manufacturing. Contaminated water from the rupture flowed through Longview's drainage system as authorities managed the environmental fallout.

cards.headline: California poll shows Becerra opening lead in governor's race
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra has pulled ahead in polling as the California gubernatorial election approaches.
cards.body:
A new poll indicates Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in California's gubernatorial race. The candidates have been making campaign stops across the state, including recent appearances in the Bay Area.

The race has shifted rapidly in recent weeks, according to political observers. Democratic Party officials say they are not concerned about the outcome of the gubernatorial contest. Voter guides are being published to help undecided Californians understand the race as the election nears.

cards.headline: DOJ charges Google employee over $1.2 million in Polymarket trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors say a Google staffer used insider information to profit on a prediction market site.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors have charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly made $1.2 million on Polymarket trades related to Google Search trends in 2025. According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information to know the outcome of his wagers before the public did.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on a prediction market platform, signaling increased government enforcement against illegal trading practices on these sites.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Paxton after Texas Senate primary
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton has mended relationships with Republican colleagues following a contentious primary victory.
cards.body:
Republicans are working to repair divisions within the party following Ken Paxton's contentious Texas Senate primary victory. The race featured sharp attacks that strained relationships among GOP members, though officials are now focused on rebuilding ties.

In the general election matchup, Democrat James Talarico is centering his campaign on Paxton's past scandals. The race will test Democratic prospects in a state that has historically favored Republicans.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Revised Card Text

Jill Biden told CBS News that she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought Joe Biden might have suffered a stroke, describing it as behavior she had never witnessed before or since.

The interview, set to air on Sunday, provides insight into her immediate concerns during the debate, which became a pivotal moment in the 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuation of southern Lebanon areas near Zahrani River
cards.teaser: The Israeli military designated swathes of southern Lebanon as combat zones and threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has issued evacuation orders for areas of southern Lebanon located south of the Zahrani River, designating them as "combat zones." The military announcement indicates an escalation of operations in the region.

Israeli officials have threatened Hezbollah with additional military strikes in the designated areas, signaling potential intensification of hostilities along the Lebanese border.

hero.headline: Oil prices rise after US strikes Iran during peace talks
hero.body:
Oil prices climbed sharply after the United States launched military strikes against Iran, marking the second attack in three days despite an ongoing ceasefire and peace negotiations between the two countries.

Brent crude rose 1.95% to $71.72 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate increased 2.12% to $66.67 per barrel by Thursday afternoon, continuing gains from overnight trading when both benchmarks jumped 4%. The rally reflects investor concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

The timing creates significant uncertainty for markets and policymakers. Oil had fallen below $100 a barrel earlier in the week on optimism that a peace deal might be reached to end the three-month conflict. That sentiment reversed once the strikes were announced, demonstrating how quickly investor expectations can shift in response to geopolitical developments.

The strikes occurred despite a six-week-old ceasefire and ongoing diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. According to market analysts, the situation reveals a dangerous complacency among some investors who may underestimate escalation risks.

"Oil markets are starting to price in higher risk as Iran remains a major producer, and more importantly, sits at the heart of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of global oil supply transits," explained Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at capital.com. Even limited disruptions to shipping lanes could trigger immediate supply shocks that ripple through global economies.

Market participants are assigning roughly a 70% probability to a potential US strike on Iran. Beyond energy markets, analysts warn that broader economic consequences could follow, including shipping delays, global supply chain disruption, and increased inflation that might influence central bank interest rate decisions.

Stock markets declined in response to the developments. In the US, major indexes opened lower, with the Dow down 0.25%, the S&P 500 down 0.35%, and the Nasdaq down 0.49%. European indexes extended losses, with the FTSE 100 down 0.6%, Germany's DAX down 0.8%, France's CAC 40 down 0.79%, and Spain's IBEX down 0.85%.

Safe haven assets also moved higher. Gold prices increased 0.23% to $4,991.58 per ounce, as investors sought protection against potential escalation.

The situation has prompted warnings from analysts about the risks of investor complacency. "This muted response suggests that investors are either sceptical of imminent escalation or confident that any conflict would be short-lived," Hathorn noted. "This complacency, however, raises the risk of a sharp repricing event. If tensions move from rhetoric to action, oil could spike rapidly, bond yields could rise on inflation fears, and equities could experience a volatility shock."

All eyes remain on the White House for any signals about whether diplomatic efforts will continue or if escalation appears likely.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading on betting platform
cards.teaser: A longtime Google worker faces charges for allegedly using internal company data to profit from bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading for allegedly using confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Spagnuolo wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and other search-related trends.

According to prosecutors, Spagnuolo profited $1.2 million from these trades because he had access to Google's confidential data before the public knew the outcomes. The charges allege he violated insider trading laws by leveraging non-public information from internal company systems to gain an unfair advantage in the prediction market.

cards.headline: Australia launches $2 billion lawsuit against 3M over contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government sued the US company over chemical contamination at defense sites from firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia has launched a record-breaking legal action against 3M, seeking over A$2 billion in damages for contamination caused by PFAS chemicals in firefighting foam. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the case, which targets pollution at defence bases across the country.

PFAS, known as "forever chemicals," persist in the environment and have been linked to health concerns. This lawsuit represents the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government against a private company.

cards.headline: Pork prices in China fall to 16-year low
cards.teaser: The drop signals weak consumer spending and oversupply in the country's hog market.
cards.body:
China's pork prices have dropped to their lowest point in 16 years, reflecting significant economic headwinds. The collapse is driven by weak consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs flooding the market faster than buyers can absorb them.

Pork serves as a critical inflation gauge in China given its central role in the national diet. The sharp price decline underscores mounting pressure on household finances and the broader challenge of excess production in the sector.

cards.headline: Chinese factories expand overseas operations globally
cards.teaser: China is establishing manufacturing facilities in other countries as its trade surplus triggers international concern.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are building factories across the world as the country's massive trade surplus creates tension with trading partners. China's trade surplus reached $1.2 trillion, prompting questions about how Beijing manages its international economic relationships.

The expansion of Chinese manufacturing abroad has raised concerns among competitors in various countries. India may benefit from the shift in global manufacturing patterns. A former Chongqing mayor called for action as China appears poised for a record trade surplus this year.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
FIFA is facing an investigation by the attorneys general of New York and New Jersey over its 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe examines allegations that fans were misled about ticket purchases and seat locations.

The investigation centers on whether FIFA violated consumer protection standards in how it marketed and sold tickets for World Cup matches. The inquiry was launched following reports from fans who received different seats than expected or encountered unclear pricing structures.

cards.headline: Space stocks rally as SpaceX IPO approaches
cards.teaser: Companies like Rocket Lab and AST saw sharp gains ahead of SpaceX's planned public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX is moving forward with plans for a major stock market debut valued at $1.75 trillion, which could make Elon Musk a trillionaire. The anticipated IPO has generated increased interest across the space sector, with related stocks experiencing gains.

The race toward SpaceX's public offering comes as competition intensifies in the tech industry, particularly around AI development. Investors are closely monitoring the IPO's progress and SpaceX's investor pitch, which includes ambitious plans like Mars colonization.

cards.headline: Tipping expectations increase in US and abroad
cards.teaser: Service workers in the US now expect 20 percent tips as the practice spreads to other countries.
cards.body:
Tipping culture in the United States has intensified, with service workers expressing dissatisfaction when gratuities fall below 20 percent. The trend is also expanding to other countries where tipping was previously less common or expected at lower rates.

The shift reflects changing norms around compensation for service industry employees. Workers in restaurants and other service positions increasingly rely on tips as a significant portion of their income, leading to higher baseline expectations for what customers should pay beyond the listed price.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million profit on Polymarket
hero.body:
Federal authorities have charged a Google engineer with insider trading after the individual made $1.2 million through bets placed on the prediction market platform Polymarket.

According to the criminal complaint, the engineer wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The charges suggest the engineer used confidential information obtained through their position at the technology company to place the wagers.

Polymarket is a prediction market platform where users can bet on the outcomes of future events, ranging from political elections to corporate announcements. The platform has grown in popularity as an alternative way to forecast events through market-based predictions.

The case marks a notable intersection between traditional insider trading enforcement and newer prediction market platforms. While insider trading prosecutions typically involve traditional stock markets, this case demonstrates that authorities are applying the same legal framework to trading on prediction markets when nonpublic information is involved.

The complaint indicates the engineer risked a substantial sum on wagers tied specifically to outcomes related to Google's annual Year in Search campaign, which highlights trending searches and cultural moments from the year. The timing and specificity of the bets apparently drew the attention of investigators.

The $1.2 million profit represents the gains allegedly made from the trades, while the $2.7 million figure reflects the total amount wagered across the related bets. The engineer would have had access to internal Google information about the campaign before it became public.

Federal insider trading laws prohibit trading securities or other instruments based on material nonpublic information. Prosecutors have increasingly applied these statutes beyond traditional stock trading to encompass various financial instruments and markets.

The case is part of ongoing efforts by financial regulators and law enforcement to monitor activity on prediction markets, which have operated in a regulatory gray area. As these platforms have gained users and trading volume, they have attracted greater scrutiny from authorities concerned about potential market manipulation and the misuse of confidential information.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over chemical contamination at defense sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US manufacturing company over firefighting foam pollution.
cards.body:
The Australian government has filed a record-breaking lawsuit against 3M, seeking more than $2 billion in damages over contamination at defense sites. The case represents the largest legal claim the government has ever brought.

The lawsuit centers on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as "forever chemicals," found in firefighting foam used at Australian military installations. These chemicals persist in the environment and accumulate over time, causing contamination concerns at the affected defense bases.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A court ruling allows the state civil rights agency to proceed with its case against the automaker, with trial set for July.
cards.body:
A California court has rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency. The ruling allows the case to move forward to trial.

The civil rights agency expressed satisfaction with the court's decision and indicated the case is expected to go to trial in July. The lawsuit alleges racial discrimination at Tesla.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker will begin customer deliveries of its new SUV model next month.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. The company has finally announced a firm date for these initial deliveries.

CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as potentially the most important product Rivian has launched to date, underscoring the vehicle's significance to the company's future lineup.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe photographed Mars, including views of the south pole, while traveling toward an asteroid destination.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby en route to its primary destination, a distant asteroid. The mission took advantage of the planet encounter to capture high-resolution images offering unique views of the red planet.

The images include detailed photographs of Mars' south pole. NASA described the views as spectacular, with the spacecraft gathering data while traveling along its trajectory toward the asteroid target.

cards.headline: Google AI tools struggle with basic spelling tasks
cards.teaser: The company's artificial intelligence systems are having difficulty spelling words including the company's own name.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence features are experiencing significant spelling problems, unable to correctly spell basic words including "Google" itself, "disregard," "stop," and "ignore." The issues have become increasingly visible to users of the company's AI-powered search tools, with the AI Overview feature appearing to perform noticeably worse in recent times.

The spelling difficulties have attracted widespread online attention and represent an embarrassing setback for the tech giant's AI capabilities, raising questions about the reliability of these tools for everyday tasks.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The Nintendo 64 game will join the subscription service's library on June 3.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will be added to Nintendo Switch Online next week. The game will become available to subscribers on June 3.

The addition expands the Nintendo 64 library available through the Switch Online service's Expansion Pack tier. Donkey Kong 64 originally released in the 1990s and is being added to the growing collection of classic N64 titles available to subscribers.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI platform
cards.teaser: The oncology-focused artificial intelligence company secured Series B funding led by Battery Ventures.
cards.body:
Triomics has secured $22 million in Series B funding to advance its artificial intelligence platform designed for oncology applications. Battery Ventures led the investment round.

The company is developing AI technology tailored specifically for cancer centers, with the new capital supporting continued development and deployment of its oncology-focused tools.

hero.headline: SEC commissioner defends conference superiority despite Big Ten's recent dominance
hero.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said his conference still stands alone as the best in college football, even as the Big Ten has won the past three national championships and holds a 4-0 record against the SEC in College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Sankey made the remarks during college football's spring meetings, a gathering that has been dominated by discussions of conference expansion and playoff structure. His comments come at a time when the Big Ten has demonstrated clear superiority in head-to-head competition.

The SEC has long positioned itself as the premier conference in college football, but recent results have challenged that narrative. The Big Ten's three consecutive national titles represent a significant shift in the sport's power dynamics.

Sankey's insistence that the SEC remains the top conference by far appears to dismiss the on-field evidence from recent seasons. The head-to-head playoff record and championship outcomes provide measurable data points that contradict his assessment.

The spring meetings have brought conference realignment and competitive balance to the forefront of college football governance. As conferences continue to expand and reshape the sport's landscape, the competitive rivalry between the SEC and Big Ten has intensified.

Sankey's defense of SEC supremacy reflects the high stakes involved in maintaining the conference's brand and recruiting advantages. Conference reputation directly impacts television revenue, recruiting, and playoff selection.

The broader context includes ongoing negotiations over playoff expansion and format. How conferences position themselves in these discussions could determine the future structure of college football's postseason.

While Sankey maintains the SEC's dominance, the Big Ten's recent success in championship games and playoff matchups suggests the balance of power in college football may be shifting. The coming seasons will determine whether the Big Ten's run continues or if the SEC can reclaim its position atop the sport.

cards.headline: Georgia coach suggests SEC could leave NCAA without playoff agreement
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart raised the possibility of the SEC essentially seceding from the NCAA if conference expansion talks do not reach a resolution.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart suggested Tuesday that the SEC could leave the NCAA if negotiations fail to produce an agreement on playoff expansion and related issues. His remarks came during college football's spring meetings, where conference expansion has been a dominant topic of discussion.

Smart's comments represent one of the most forceful statements yet about how far conferences might go to protect their interests as ongoing negotiations continue.

cards.headline: Hurricanes take 3-1 series lead with shutout over Canadiens
cards.teaser: Frederik Andersen stopped 18 shots in his third playoff shutout this postseason as Carolina moved within one win of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Frederik Andersen made 18 saves to shut out the Canadiens and give the Hurricanes a 3-1 series lead in the Eastern Conference finals. The victory puts Carolina one win away from advancing to the Stanley Cup Final.

Andersen has now recorded three shutouts in 12 playoff games this postseason. His performance helped the Hurricanes take command of the series as they seek their first trip to the Final in several years.

cards.headline: Phillies pitcher breaks franchise scoreless innings record set in 1911
cards.teaser: Cristopher Sanchez extended his scoreless streak to 44 innings, surpassing Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander's Phillies record.
cards.body:
Cristopher Sánchez set a new Phillies franchise record on Wednesday by extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, a record that had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's accomplishment breaks a benchmark that endured for over a century, solidifying his place in franchise history alongside one of baseball's greatest pitchers.

cards.headline: Oklahoma athletic director sees playoff expansion as path to revive Bedlam rivalry
cards.teaser: Roger Denny said College Football Playoff expansion could enable tougher nonconference scheduling and potentially restore the Oklahoma-Oklahoma State series.
cards.body:
Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny said playoff expansion could create opportunities for scheduling stronger nonconference games and potentially reviving the Bedlam rivalry against Oklahoma State. The annual series between the in-state rivals has been discontinued.

Denny suggested that an expanded playoff format might reduce the risks associated with scheduling difficult nonconference opponents. This could make it feasible to restore traditional rivalry games that were dropped due to conference realignment and scheduling constraints.

cards.headline: Von Miller lobbies Broncos for return to Denver
cards.teaser: The former Super Bowl MVP said he will play in 2026 and has already contacted Sean Payton about rejoining his former team.
cards.body:
Von Miller said Wednesday he is "for sure" playing football in the 2026 season and has already reached out to Denver coach Sean Payton about returning to the Broncos. Miller spent much of his career with Denver before playing for other teams.

The Super Bowl MVP winner remains one of the franchise's most accomplished players. His outreach to Payton signals his interest in potentially reuniting with his former team.

cards.headline: Arizona forward Koa Peat stays in NBA draft
cards.teaser: The projected first-round pick will not return to college basketball, sources told ESPN.
cards.body:
Arizona forward Koa Peat is staying in the NBA draft rather than returning to college basketball. The projected first-round pick made his decision official on Wednesday, according to ESPN sources.

By keeping his name in the draft, Peat is forgoing the opportunity to maintain his college eligibility and pursue a professional career instead.

cards.headline: Top transfer portal player withdraws from NBA draft
cards.teaser: Milan Momcilovic, formerly of Iowa State, will return to college basketball instead of pursuing a professional career.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, the top-ranked player available in the transfer portal, has withdrawn from the NBA draft and will return to college basketball for the upcoming season. The former Iowa State forward made the decision through his agents, according to ESPN.

Momcilovic's choice to remain in college rather than pursue the professional ranks marks a significant development in the current transfer portal cycle, as he was the most coveted uncommitted player available to programs nationwide.

hero.headline: Spielberg opposes AI in creative filmmaking decisions
hero.body:
Director Steven Spielberg expressed opposition to using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson. Spielberg said he does not want AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood.

The director distinguished between AI applications he supports and those he opposes. He said he believes AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues.

Spielberg stated his objection to AI involvement in creative decisions. He said he does not support AI being used as the final word on anything creative in filmmaking. The director drew a clear boundary on where AI should not be applied in the entertainment industry.

The podcast appearance marks the latest instance of a major Hollywood figure weighing in on AI use in entertainment production. Spielberg has directed numerous films over several decades and remains an influential voice in the industry.

The director's comments come as the entertainment industry continues to debate the appropriate role of artificial intelligence in content creation. Production companies and studios have been exploring various AI applications, while creators and unions have raised concerns about the technology's impact on creative work.

Spielberg did not elaborate on specific AI tools or applications beyond his general opposition to the technology making creative decisions. He focused his objection on AI serving as a decision-making authority in creative matters rather than as a tool supporting human creators.

cards.headline: Film Obsession posts rare second-weekend box office increase
cards.teaser: The horror film achieved a second-weekend box office spike, a performance not seen since Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
The film Obsession posted a box office increase in its second weekend of release, becoming a breakout hit. The performance marked a rare achievement for theatrical releases.

The second-weekend spike represented a pattern not seen at the box office since Sound of Freedom. Multiple entertainment outlets described the film's performance as making history and becoming a record-breaking horror release.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight wins fourth consecutive News Emmy
cards.teaser: ABC World News Tonight With David Muir took the outstanding live news program prize for the fourth year in a row.
cards.body:
ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmy ceremony, the most of any outlet. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir received the outstanding live news program award, marking its fourth consecutive win in the category.

National Geographic won seven News Emmys, the second-highest total. The Nat Geo program Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller accounted for the bulk of those wins. Both ABC News and National Geographic are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Morris Day denies participation in National Mall Freedom 250 concert
cards.teaser: The musician said he and the Time will not perform at the June event despite being listed in the official lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied that he and the Time will perform at a Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall, calling reports of his participation rumors. Organizers had announced him as a headliner for a June 27 show as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

The event has generated debate among fans and performers. Other acts advertised for the celebration include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, C+C Music Factory, and Milli Vanilli. The concert is part of a celebration marking America's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Student journalist criticizes CBS News in scholarship acceptance speech
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos used his Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship acceptance to address CBS News editorial direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School, addressed CBS News during his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy ceremony. Campos said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

The Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship is named after the longtime CBS journalist. Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award to Campos at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism of recent clothing choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed backlash over outfits that internet commenters said infantilized and sexualized her.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo commented on public reaction to her recent clothing selections. Internet commenters had accused her outfits of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer.

Rodrigo said people should not be responsible for others sexualizing them. The singer addressed the debate over her fashion choices directly in response to the online criticism.

cards.headline: Leonora Carrington psychiatric confinement painting to be exhibited publicly
cards.teaser: A work by the artist created during psychiatric confinement will be shown for the first time.
cards.body:
A painting by artist Leonora Carrington created during a period of psychiatric confinement will go on public display. The work has not been exhibited before.

Carrington was a surrealist artist and writer. The exhibition marks the first time this particular work from her confinement period will be shown to the public.

cards.headline: The Beaches song surges 888 percent after appearing in Off Campus
cards.teaser: The band's 2023 track Edge of the Earth went viral again following its use in a scene from the show.
cards.body:
Canadian band The Beaches saw their 2023 song Edge of the Earth experience an 888 percent increase in streaming. The spike followed the song's inclusion in a scene from the show Off Campus.

The track was featured in a scene involving characters Hannah and Garrett. This marks another viral moment for the band, which has previously gained attention through online platforms.

hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported the investigation on Wednesday night. The probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury while speaking at a deposition as part of her two civil lawsuits against Trump.

Carroll sued Trump twice in civil court. The first lawsuit alleged defamation after Trump denied her allegations of sexual assault. A second lawsuit made similar claims. Both cases resulted in verdicts against Trump, with juries awarding Carroll substantial damages.

The investigation represents a significant shift in the legal battles between Trump and Carroll. Previously, Trump faced civil liability in courts over his denials of Carroll's allegations. The criminal probe now places Carroll herself under scrutiny by federal prosecutors.

Perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a witness knowingly made false statements under oath during official proceedings. Depositions in civil lawsuits carry the same legal weight as courtroom testimony, and witnesses face potential criminal penalties for lying.

The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the investigation. Federal prosecutors in criminal cases typically decline to confirm or deny ongoing investigations until charges are filed.

Carroll's attorneys have not issued public statements about the probe. The investigation's scope and timeline remain unknown.

The development adds another layer to the years-long legal conflict between Trump and Carroll. Her initial allegations dated back decades but became public when she published a memoir detailing the alleged assault. Trump's denials led to the defamation lawsuits that ultimately resulted in the depositions now under investigation.

The criminal investigation proceeds separately from the civil cases, which have concluded with judgments against Trump. Federal investigators will examine deposition transcripts and other evidence to determine whether Carroll's statements meet the legal threshold for perjury charges.

cards.headline: U.S. military shoots down Iranian drones, strikes launch site in Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The U.S. military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station preparing to launch a fifth drone.
cards.body:
The U.S. military intercepted four Iranian attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. Iran's military had directed the drones at a commercial ship in the strait.

This confrontation represents the second such clash within 48 hours. The incident comes as the U.S. and Iran continue negotiating to resolve their conflict. President Trump's recent statements indicate he is maintaining strict demands in the negotiations.

cards.headline: Former federal judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement creating a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed normal judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement directly with the president.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged "victims of lawfare and weaponization." The judges question whether proper legal procedures were followed in reaching the agreement, seeking court investigation into how the settlement was structured and executed.

cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel let activist Mahmoud Khalil stay free while he takes his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court.

cards.headline: Senate Republican leaders endorse Ken Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders moved to unite behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Sen. John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone before publicly endorsing him on a radio show, signaling party unity after a divisive primary fight between Paxton and Sen. John Cornyn.

Republican leaders are emphasizing to major donors that winning Texas is critical to maintaining Senate control in the upcoming November elections. The effort represents an attempt to move past the bitter primary campaign and present a unified front heading into the general election.

cards.headline: Sen. Andy Kim responds to Homeland Security secretary over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Sen. Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized the senator for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin said Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim said the incident was never about him personally. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement and conditions at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to supply Patriot interceptors
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and Congress to provide Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
